error.title: Manifest validation failed
error.hint: The manifests below failed JSON Schema validation and were skipped. Fix them and re-scan.

install.title: Install
install.preflightPassed: All checks passed — ready to install
install.preflightHint: These checks report every reason that would fail up front, instead of letting you hit the wall halfway through.
install.cancelRequested: Cancel requested — finishing the current item…
install.targetDirHint: Per-user directory — no admin rights, no system PATH edits

pending.title: An install run was left unfinished
pending.body: Plan {{id}} still has {{count}} unfinished items. Resuming re-runs only the unfinished ones; completed items are skipped.
pending.invalid: The previous install plan is no longer valid: {{reason}}. Please select again.

preset.label: Presets:
preset.importHint: Paste a shared preset JSON. A preset is just a selection — it contains no commands.
preset.missingTools: {{count}} entries no longer exist in the manifest and will be skipped

settings.title: Settings
settings.mirrorPreferenceHint: Affects try order only; failures still fall back to other sources
settings.proxyHint: http://host:port; empty means follow the system
settings.activateHint: Wire the version into user PATH and env vars so a new terminal just works
settings.restorePointHint: Requires admin; only meaningful when machine-scope items are selected
settings.mirrorsHint: Turning one off reverts to the official source (it removes exactly the block devkit wrote, leaving your other settings alone). Locations: npm → .npmrc; pip → pip.ini; Go → GOPROXY; Maven → .m2/settings.xml; Gradle → .gradle/init.gradle; cargo → .cargo/config.toml; conda → .condarc; NuGet → NuGet.Config; Docker → .docker/daemon.json (restart Docker).
settings.offlineHint: Bundle the selected tools plus checksums into a folder for offline machines
settings.pathBackup: Original user PATH backed up to {{path}}
settings.pathBackupNone: User PATH has not been modified yet, so there is no backup
settings.hotUpdateHint: Fetch the latest versions and checksums remotely. Only version/URL/SHA-256/size/mirrors are accepted; install commands and activation always come from the local manifest.
settings.hotUpdateUrlHint: Point this at your own manifest index once published; empty disables it
settings.hotUpdateAutoHint: One background fetch at startup; failures never block the app
settings.systemHint: Each item is inspected first, then written. Nothing that can be done per-user asks for admin; HKLM writes trigger one UAC prompt.
settings.updateFeedHint: Points at a latest.json or latest.yml; empty disables the check
settings.storageHint: Version dirs, switch links and the download cache are bulk artifacts (measured up to several GB) and can be moved to another drive.
settings.dataRootFromEnv: Currently from the DEVKIT_DATA_ROOT environment variable (not editable here)
settings.dataRootEnvLocked: Locked by an environment variable — change DEVKIT_DATA_ROOT instead.
settings.dataRootWarn: This only affects future installs: versions already installed under the old root are neither moved nor detected.

installed.title: Installed (devkit-managed version dirs)
installed.hint: Uninstall only removes devkit version dirs; existing system installs are untouched
installed.empty: Nothing has been installed through devkit yet
installed.activateHint: Switch to this version: repoints the junction and user PATH, files stay put
installed.notActivatable: No activation declared for this version
installed.uninstallDesc: Removes the version directory; if it is the active one it is deactivated first
installed.scopeNote: Location: %USERPROFILE%\.devkit\versions\<tool>\<version>\. Uninstall does not roll back other system changes.

detail.versionsHint: Every URL and checksum below comes from the official channel and is verified at install time.
detail.noHash: No checksum declared for this version (it will not appear as installable)

vscode.title: Recommended VS Code extensions
vscode.hint: Extensions change editor behaviour, so this is a recommendation list only — pick what you want. Each install runs code --install-extension.
vscode.unavailableHint: Once VS Code is installed (or installed and activated through devkit), you can install extensions here in one click.
